newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was lower against the dollar in late Monday trading, dealers said.
They said the rupiah firmed up briefly at midday as overnight money suddenly rose to 21.0 percent from 9.0 percent.
But they said technical factor and early ample liquidity was responsible for rupiah weakening from the morning, while some attributed it to a tight dollar market.
"I don't think the dollar market was tight. You can still find some offers around. It's the net open position which drives people to sell swaps rather than borrow dollars," one said.

The Japanese bank dealer said off-balance sheets limitations had caused operators to unload swaps, sending overnight swaps reeling into negative territory although there were still some premiums available in converting dollar borrowings.
Overnight swap was at -0.1/-0.05 and tom/next at 0.15/0.19.

Purchases of value today dollars drove overnight dollar higher and other maturities followed, dealers said. But overnight dollar later fell to 6.0 percent from 6.75 percent in the morning. Some dealers had said earlier the phenomenon was only temporary because operators had established long dollar positions last week on ample rupiah supply.
Spot rupiah was at 2,414.50/14.70 at 0935 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,410.50/11.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,414.3/14.5 and 2,412.0/13.0, respectively.
Dealers said swap rates softened slightly from the morning.
One-month swaps eased off to 10.1/10.25 from 10.25/10.50, two to 21.5/22.25 from 22.0/23.0, three to 33.0/34.5 from 33.75/34.50 and six to 69.5/70.75 from 70.5/71.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,402/2,594 and the conversion band at 2,402/2,450 on Monday.
The market was closed last Friday for a Muslim holiday.
